documents.title: AI Course Policies and Assignment Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide rule on whether students may use AI; it says the syllabus template will offer "pre-set AI policy templates, including no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI" and that the integrity policy's emphasis on "unauthorized" use "recognizes instructors' authority". Decision handed to instructors, with tiers.
documents.summary: Faculty Excellence guidance for instructors writing AI course policies. It announces syllabus-template AI policy options (none, some, unrestricted), reiterates that the Academic Integrity policy treats unauthorized AI use as dishonesty and requires citing AI, and urges instructors to disclose their own AI use.

units.why: The page advises instructors that "recognizing the prevalence of AI use is crucial" when crafting policy; this is advice to instructors at the design phase, closest to faculty learning about AI (P63), not a student rule.
units.anchor: recognizing the prevalence of AI use is crucial
units.frag_start: As instructors craft their AI policies
units.policy: Instructors recognize the prevalence of AI use as they craft their AI policies.
units.fit_note: Advises awareness of AI prevalence rather than workshops or consultations.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Source: 'As instructors craft their AI policies, recognizing the prevalence of AI use is crucial.' This is advice to instructors before setting policy, so it is a real statement; kept as should. P63 includes advice that instructors learn about AI before setting course policy; fit_note kept.

units.why: "AI output reads as authoritative" yet only an informed person "can well assess its accuracy or usefulness": AI output must be judged for accuracy, so P31 (verify output).
units.anchor: can well assess its accuracy or usefulness
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B student. The source sentence is a general statement about AI output addressed to instructors drafting policy, not a rule binding students, so all. Phase, modality and type P31 agreed.

units.why: "Students new to a discipline are likely to over-estimate AI's accuracy" and "will need careful guidance and education"; novices cannot judge AI output, so P42 rather than P31 because the focus is on beginners.
units.anchor: Students new to a discipline are likely to over-estimate AI's accuracy and usefulness
units.policy: Students new to a discipline are likely to over-estimate AI's accuracy and usefulness, and will need careful guidance and education to develop AI critical thinking.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P42, phase, modality; actor differed (A all, B student). The sentence is about students new to a discipline, so student. A left policy null, B normalized; kept B because the anchor omits the careful guidance and education clause, and the normalization is verbatim from the source.

units.why: "the Montclair Syllabus template will come with a designated field for AI policy" is a university mechanism making each syllabus carry an AI statement; closest is P09, though it is a template field, not an explicit mandate.
units.anchor: the Montclair Syllabus template will come with a designated field for AI policy
units.fit_note: Describes a template field for AI policy; does not state that filling it is mandatory.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P09, admin, before-course, informs; the source only says the syllabus template will come with a designated field for AI policy, no mandate, so informs with fit_note.

units.why: Faculty "will be able to choose from pre-set AI policy templates, including no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI": named tiers of use, so P05.
units.anchor: no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI
units.frag_start: Faculty will be able to choose
units.resolution_why: Full agreement: the named templates 'no use of AI, some use of AI, or unrestricted use of AI' are tiers (P05).

units.why: The page lists "Citing AI", "Montclair faculty statements" and "a larger national collection of statements" as faculty resources for drafting policies, which is support for instructors in setting policy (P63).
units.fit_note: Resources are sample statements and a citing guide rather than workshops or consultations.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The page lists 'Citing AI', 'Montclair faculty statements' and 'a larger national collection of statements' under 'Faculty Resources:'. It is a real offer of support for instructors writing policies; kept as informs under P63 with fit_note. B did not code it.

units.why: Faculty may "write their own AI policy" instead of a template: the decision rests with the instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: or to write their own AI policy
units.frag_start: Faculty will be able to choose
units.policy: Faculty may write their own AI policy instead of choosing a template.
units.resolution_why: Agreement on all codes. A had unit_stance permit, B neutral; the passage only gives faculty the option to write their own policy, so neutral. B's normalized policy follows the source ('or to write their own AI policy').

units.why: The Academic Integrity policy lists "unauthorized assistance... generative artificial intelligence (AI)... to generate a work product" as dishonest behavior: unauthorized AI use is misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: unauthorized assistance or unauthorized materials from any source
units.frag_start: includes as an example of dishonest behavior
units.policy: The University's Academic Integrity policy lists unauthorized assistance or unauthorized materials from any source, including generative AI, used to generate a work product as an example of dishonest behavior.
units.resolution_why: Full agreement on P36, student, when-misuse, must-not. The source lists unauthorized assistance including generative AI as dishonest behavior, a classification. B's normalized policy kept because the anchor omits the generative AI part.

units.why: "The emphasis on unauthorized recognizes instructors' authority to establish clear expectations about whether and how these tools may be used": the rule is left to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: recognizes instructors' authority to establish clear expectations about whether and how
units.frag_end: may be used in their courses.
units.fit_note: Also says instructors should set clear expectations (communication).
units.resolution_why: Phase differed: A general, B course-start. The sentence explains why the integrity policy says 'unauthorized' (instructor authority); it states a principle and does not tell anyone to communicate at course start, so general. P04 and informs agreed; B's fit_note kept.

units.why: "Cite a generative AI tool whenever work created by the tool is paraphrased, quoted, or incorporated": students must cite AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: Cite a generative AI tool whenever work created by the tool is paraphrased, quoted
units.frag_start: Cite a generative AI tool whenever
units.resolution_why: Full agreement on P24, student, during-work, must: 'Cite a generative AI tool whenever work created by the tool is paraphrased, quoted, or incorporated'.

units.why: "If generative AI was used to edit one's own prose, the use of the tool for this function should be acknowledged": acknowledgment of AI editing, which is disclosure (P24), though specific to prose.
units.anchor: the use of the tool for this function should be acknowledged in the work
units.fit_note: Specific to AI used for editing prose; coder A coded P18 (separate prose rules), but the rule is an acknowledgment duty.
units.resolution_why: Type differed: A P18, B P24. The sentence 'the use of the tool for this function should be acknowledged in the work' is an acknowledgment rule, which P24 defines ('disclose, acknowledge, or cite'). P18 is for rules on what prose uses are allowed; this neither permits nor restricts, it requires acknowledgment. So P24 with fit_note.

units.why: "Disclose and explain how you use AI to support your teaching": instructors are told to disclose their own AI use, so P47.
units.anchor: Disclose and explain how you use AI to support your teaching
units.resolution_why: Phase differed (A during-work, B general) and unit_stance (A permit, B encourage). The advice is to instructors about their own teaching AI use, not student work in progress, so general. It presumes AI use is acceptable if disclosed, and says 'should', so permit. P47, instructor, should agreed.

units.why: "Setting an example of disclosing and explaining impactful AI use would be extremely educational for students, modeling professional behavior and ethics": rationale for instructor disclosure; coded P47, not P44, since it concerns instructors modeling.
units.anchor: modeling professional behavior and ethics around AI use for them
units.fit_note: Gives the educational rationale (modeling professional behavior and ethics) for instructor disclosure; coder A coded P44 (AI as a professional skill), but the passage is about instructors modeling their own disclosure.
units.resolution_why: Type differed: A P44, B P47. The sentence is the reason given for instructors disclosing their own AI use ('Setting an example of disclosing and explaining ... modeling professional behavior'). P44 is about teaching students effective AI use as a skill; this is not, so P47 with fit_note.

notes: Single included document; consensus of 13 units (11 matched, 1 only-A and 1 only-B, both kept). A draft university AI Innovation and Responsible Use Policy was expected in Fall 2026 but is not yet available (coder A note).
